sections.html:
Jessamine County's seat, Nicholasville, is a home rule city lying south of Lexington. The head count was 28,015 in 2010 and 31,093 in 2020, with a federal estimate of 33,857 for mid-2025, up 8.8 percent from the 2020 base. Over the half century from 1970 to 2020 the population multiplied by roughly 5.4, enough to rank the city tenth in Kentucky.

Rapid growth brings plenty of commuters. For 2020-2024 the Census lists 12,131 households, 58.2 percent of them owner-occupied, a $226,800 median home value and a 24-minute average trip to work.

sections.h2: What is the setting of a Nicholasville house?
sections.html:
The town was founded in 1798 and incorporated in 1837, named for a colonel who helped shape Kentucky's first constitution. Downtown sits about six miles south of the Fayette County line, and the city covers roughly 13 square miles of land. A partly channelized stream called Town Fork runs underneath downtown and drains to Jessamine Creek, and there are small artificial ponds such as Lake Mingo.

The Bluegrass climate is humid subtropical at its northern edge, with hot, humid summers, cool winters and four distinct seasons. Camp Nelson National Monument is close by, the Young House carries a National Register listing, and the Kentucky Wine and Vine Fest was named the official wine festival of Kentucky by the General Assembly in 2014.

  • Nicholasville is a logistics and commuter link between Lexington and Garrard County.
  • Jessamine County Schools provides public education, including Nicholasville, Brookside, Red Oak, Rosenwald-Dunbar and Hattie C. Warner elementary schools.
  • City government is a commission of a mayor and four commissioners, elected at large, who also run city departments.

sections.h2: How does Nicholasville compare with Lexington for a seller?
sections.html:
Many Nicholasville owners measure their house against Lexington, six miles north. The Census 2020-2024 figures show the two sides of that comparison.

  • Median home value: $226,800 in Nicholasville, $293,500 in Lexington-Fayette.
  • Median gross rent: $1,147 against $1,164, nearly the same.
  • Owner-occupied rate: 58.2 percent against 53.8 percent, so Nicholasville has fewer tenants.
  • Median household income: $68,503 against $69,479.
  • Mean commute: 24.0 minutes against 20.9 minutes.

In plain terms, a buyer pays about $66,700 less at the median here than across the line, yet rents are almost identical. That gap is why investors watch Nicholasville and why owner-occupants who want a Lexington job without Lexington prices keep arriving.

Other Census measures describe a family-oriented place: 25.0 percent of residents are under 18, 14.1 percent are 65 or older, 1,532 are veterans, and 90.0 percent of households have a broadband subscription. Public school students attend Jessamine County Schools, and the Jessamine County Public Library is based in the city.

sections.h2: Who handles code complaints and permits in Nicholasville?
sections.html:
Nicholasville has its own Code Enforcement office at 717 N. Main Street, and complaints go in through a form on the city website. A Code Enforcement Board also hears matters, and residents can apply to serve on it. If you have received a notice about tall grass, debris or an unsafe structure, answer it before you list or accept an offer.

For building and electrical permits, ask the city Planning and Zoning office which approvals your project needs, and keep copies of finished permits to hand to a buyer. Unpermitted work is a common reason a conventional sale stalls, so tell a buyer about it up front.

sections.h2: What does it cost to hold a house in Nicholasville?
sections.html:
Owners who carry a mortgage here spend a median $1,410 each month on housing, and owners with no mortgage spend $507. Tenants pay a median $1,147 in gross rent. Households take in a median $68,503 a year, 13.1 percent of residents are below the poverty line, and 26.9 percent of adults over 25 have a four-year degree.

In the 2020 census, 4.8 percent of the city's 12,356 housing units stood empty; the vacancy rate was 1.2 percent for owned homes and 4.9 percent for rentals. Few owner-occupied houses stood empty. Children under 18 live in 36.5 percent of households, the median age is 35.7, and the typical household has 2.63 people.

Retail sales in the city totaled $976,312,000 in 2022, or $30,554 per capita, compared with $23,150 per capita for Lexington-Fayette. City commission meetings take place twice a month, and a seller with a rezoning or street question can ask the city for the next meeting date.

sections.h2: Where is a Nicholasville deed recorded, and what is owed?
sections.html:
Deeds and mortgages for the city are recorded by the Jessamine County Clerk, who also keeps the county's property records. The main office is at 101 North Main Street and opens weekdays from eight in the morning until four in the afternoon; a Wilmore branch keeps shorter hours. The number is (859) 885-4161.

KRS 142.050 makes the seller pay the state transfer tax, and the clerk collects it before taking the deed. The price is 50 cents per $500 block. The clerk keeps five percent of the take as a collection fee and sends the remainder to the county treasurer.

No tax applies to a token-price deed between parent and child, a delinquent-tax sale, a foreclosure, or a deed that avoids foreclosure.

sections.h2: What should a Nicholasville owner know about property tax?
sections.html:
The Jessamine County PVA values the county's real estate, and its website lists the 2025-2026 homestead and disability exemption as $49,100. Owners who are 65 or older, or disabled, can apply through the PVA, and the exemption lowers the taxable value rather than the bill itself.

The closing agent usually divides the year's bill between buyer and seller, so request the proration math ahead of time. If a bill on an inherited house has gone unpaid, ask the County Clerk's delinquent tax desk for the amount owed before you agree on a closing date.

sections.h2: Which Nicholasville sellers tend to choose cash?
sections.html:
Cash appeals to an owner who wants a firm closing date more than the last few thousand dollars. A town of 33,857 has plenty of buyers, yet a troubled house can still linger.

  • A home from an estate, with heirs far away and no appetite for fixing it up.
  • A rental whose tenant has left, leaving work to be done before it can be shown.
  • A property carrying a code complaint or work done without a permit.
  • An owner relocating on a short timeline to or from the Lexington area.

Owners relocating for a Lexington-area job often work to a fixed date, and a cash deal can close on the day you pick. Camp Nelson, the wine festival and the commuter roads draw visitors, but none of that changes the paperwork a sale requires. Get terms in writing, compare the net with a listing once repairs and agent fees are subtracted, and ask the title company to confirm payoff figures first.

faqs.q: How many people live in Nicholasville?
faqs.a: The 2020 census recorded 31,093, and the Census Bureau's mid-2025 estimate is 33,857. The city has about 14.6 square miles of land.

faqs.q: Which office holds a Nicholasville deed?
faqs.a: The Jessamine County Clerk at 101 North Main Street. Transfer tax is paid there before the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: What tax would a $226,800 Nicholasville sale owe?
faqs.a: $227. Kentucky charges 50 cents per $500 of price under KRS 142.050, and 454 blocks result after rounding up. The seller pays.

faqs.q: What should I do about a Nicholasville code notice?
faqs.a: File a response through the Code Enforcement page or at 717 N. Main Street. Settle the notice before you pick a closing date.

faqs.q: Is there a tax break for older Jessamine County owners?
faqs.a: Yes. Owners 65 or older, or disabled, can apply through the PVA for the homestead exemption, shown as $49,100 for 2025-2026. It cuts assessed value, not the bill directly.
